title: Polyglot Sparse Probe & Embedset Sanity Notes
content:
Overview:
This is a working note for a compact, language-diverse embedset probe used during model onboarding and regression checks. The goal: fast, low-effort sanity and regression catching for embedding models that we plan to serve (hosted/dedicated/private). This doc intentionally trades breadth for quick actionable signals — target run time < 30min per model and human-reviewable failures.

Goals:
- Validate semantic separation for simple cross-lingual equivalents and common near-duplicates.
- Detect catastrophic clustering failures (collapse, severe degenerate clusters).
- Surface degrade-of-quality signals for typical semantic-search queries in 6 priority languages.
- Provide a reproducible checklist for engineers onboarding a new embedding model or quantized variant.

Scope and constraints:
- Small focused probe: ~1.2k vectors total (roughly 200 per language + 100 synthetic/edge cases).
- Languages: en, es, fr, de, pt, zh (priority), with some ad-hoc examples in ru and hi where helpful.
- Document-level and short-phrase queries included.
- No human label budget assumed for first-pass; use label heuristics (id-match, near-duplicate flags) and small manual spot checks.

Embedset composition (high level):
- LangCore (6 langs): 6 x 180 = 1080 items. Each item: (id, canonical_text, lang, source_tag).
- NearDupCluster: 40 cluster seeds x 3 paraphrases each -> 120 items (typical cluster size small to detect collapse).
- LongDocAnchors: 80 long-form passages (300-800 tokens simulated snippets) to test length-sensitivity.
- Noise / Shell: 20 nonsense / code-snippet items to detect unrelated nearest neighbors.
- Total target ~1300 items.

Sampling plan and provenance:
- Prefer real sources when available: public QA pairs, multilingual news snippets, CCNet filtered paragraphs, internal doc snippets (low sensitivity).
- Where privacy is a concern, synthesize paraphrases using controlled templates.
- Stratify by length: short (<10 tokens), medium (10-40), long (>40). Aim for 40/50/10 percent distribution within each language.

Probe categories and example probes (small sample):
- Cross-lingual equivalence (should be nearest neighbors across languages):
  - EN id: en-0421: "How do I reset my password?"
  - ES id: es-0421: "¿Cómo puedo restablecer mi contraseña?"
  - FR id: fr-0421: "Comment réinitialiser mon mot de passe ?"
- Short paraphrase near-duplicates (cluster test):
  - seed: ND-013: "cheap headphones under $50"
  - paraphrase A: "best budget earbuds less than fifty dollars"
  - paraphrase B: "headphones for under fifty bucks"
- Semantic drift / long-form anchor:
  - LD-201: 400-token product manual excerpt about "battery safety and disposal" (should not be nearest to consumer price queries)
- Multilingual short queries (Zh example):
  - ZH-033: "如何更改账单地址" (How to change billing address)

Metrics and quick thresholds (smoke-check style):
- Nearest Neighbor Recall@1 for cross-lingual pairs: expect >= 0.6 for production-grade.
- MRR for paraphrase cluster retrieval: target >= 0.55 on probe set.
- Cluster silhouette (on the small near-dup clusters): expect > 0.12. If silhouette < 0 or very low, investigate collapse.
- Noise contamination: fraction of top-5 neighbors for noise items that are non-noise should be < 0.25.
- Embedding norm inspection: check global vector norm distribution and per-quantization anomalies (median, 10th/90th percentiles). Large spikes or many zeros -> fail.

Manual labeling protocol (for spot checks):
- Select 20 random items failing any automated threshold 
- For each, label whether top-5 neighbors are: exact-duplicate / paraphrase / same-intent / different-intent / unrelated.
- Record labels in spreadsheet sheet: probe_id, model, run_date, neighbor_rank, neighbor_id, label, notes

Sanity run checklist (one-liner commands we run locally):
- 1) Provision model on dev infra (use small batch size)
  - python tools/run_embed_batch.py --model redwood/embed-small --input probe/langcore.json --out runs/redwood-embed-small-v1.json
- 2) Quick NN check (approx):
  - python tools/knn_probe.py --emb runs/redwood-embed-small-v1.json --k 5 --metrics recall-at-1,mrr,silhouette --out runs/sanity-redwood-embed-small-v1.json
- 3) Vector norm dump:
  - python tools/vec_stats.py --emb runs/redwood-embed-small-v1.json --out runs/norms-redwood-embed-small-v1.txt

Baseline models to run in onboarding order:
- redwood/embedding-compact-1 (float16)
- open/fast-embed-1 (float16)
- redwood/embedding-compact-1-8bit (quantized) -> check for collapsing norms
- Any customer-provided variant (only after baseline runs)

Preliminary results (example format for engineer notes):
- Model: redwood/embedding-compact-1  run: 2024-11-13
  - Recall@1 (cross-lingual pairs): 0.67
  - MRR (paraphrase clusters): 0.58
  - Silhouette (near-dup clusters): 0.14
  - Noise contamination top-5: 0.18
  - Notes: OK baseline. Quantized 8-bit run later to confirm behavior.

Failure modes to watch for (observed historically):
- Quantized variants collapsing to low-norm vectors: many neighbors identical across distinct ids.
- Permuted tokenization mismatch for zh/ja pairs leading to poor cross-lingual recall.
- Long-docs being pulled in as top-1 for short queries due to dense mixing of topic words.

Open questions / experiments to add:
- Add an intentional domain-shift set (API docs vs consumer docs) to see routing sensitivity.
- Quick eval of cosine vs dot-product similarity for quantized models.
- Try small length-normalization post-processing for long-doc anchor mitigation.

Ownership and next steps:
- Maya Chen: finalize embedset generation scripts and check-in seed data (due 2024-11-20).
- Diego Alvarez: run baseline models and attach run outputs to linked PR (due 2024-11-27).
- Priya Nair: coordinate spot-label round (5-10 labels) and summarize in spreadsheet (due 2024-12-04).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- add short README for folder layout: probe/langcore.json, probe/longdocs.json, probe/neardups.json
- canonical id scheme: <lang>-NNNN for LangCore, ND-### for near-dup, LD-### for long docs
- instrument embed eval pipeline to auto-fail on: zero vector fraction > 0.05 OR recall@1 < 0.4

References / useful links:
- Confluence embedset registry (see linked_artifacts)
- quick knn util: github.com/redwood-inference/embed-eval/tools/knn_probe.py
- Jira task: JIRA-ENG-2147 (onboarding checklist)

Appendix A: Minimal JSON record example for probe items (one-line):
- {"id": "en-0421", "text": "How do I reset my password?", "lang": "en", "source": "support-snippets"}

Appendix B: quick manual spot-check examples (to paste into spreadsheet):
- en-0421 neighbors: es-0421 (paraphrase), en-1102 (different-intent), nd-013-a (unrelated)
- nd-013 seed cluster should have all 3 paraphrases within top-3 neighbors for each other

End of note.

(working doc; will convert to proper PRD/checklist after one full onboarding execution)
